facts.text: In mid-April the lower slope is a burn scar full of charred fallen logs that tear and blacken clothing; expect long scrambling over deadfall.
Ticks are numerous on the lower slope in mid-April; check clothing and neck after the descent.
In early April the snow line sits near 4,000 ft, so the first 3,000 ft is bare brush; by early May the boulder field above the burn is clear and snow starts near 4,800 ft.
On a warm early-May day, start in the dark around 3 am: the brush stretch is cool and the basin snow is still firm at sunrise.

notes: The south-side tracks split into two lines: the east-side ridge line (2487652, and 1582750 in January) and a west-side basin variant (the others). Our route text describes the ridge line (saddle then ridge), so four of the six tracks follow the variant, which may deserve its own route. The party on 2487652 left the line on the way down and had to rappel a cliff to SR 20.
